finding.evidence: POST /cart with price=1 gives a 1 € line for a 120 € product
finding.description: The price is read from the form instead of the catalogue.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: client-side-price (The price is read from the form instead of the catalogue. Evidence: POST /cart with price=1 gives a 1 € line for a 120 € product). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Concrete fix: do not use client-supplied price. Accept only product ID + quantity from POST /cart, Validate on the server even when the browser checks the same fields, and Always Re-derive Security-relevant Values Server-side — if a request value influences price assume the client made it up and recalculate line and order totals from the trusted server-side catalogue.

sources.contribution: Client-only checks: Validate on the server even when the browser checks the same fields.
Always Re-derive Security-relevant Values Server-side: if a value in the request influences price, access, ownership, or state, assume the client made it up

verification.claim: Client-only checks: Validate on the server even when the browser checks the same fields.

verification.claim: Always Re-derive Security-relevant Values Server-side: if a value in the request influences price, access, ownership, or state, assume the client made it up
verification.detail: if a value in the request influences price, access, ownership, or state, assume the client made it up and recompute it from trusted data.

fix.summary: Ignore client-supplied price and re-derive cart line price from server-side PRODUCTS catalogue by id.
fix.risk: POSTs with unknown/invalid id now add nothing instead of a custom-priced line.
